html:
A writer born in Cusco, son of a Spanish conquistador and an Inca noblewoman, whose Royal Commentaries of the Incas told the story of the Inca Empire to Europe. He is often called the first great writer of mixed Spanish and Indigenous descent in the Americas.

He grew up speaking Quechua among his mother's relatives, heard their stories of the Inca past, and saw the civil wars among the conquistadors. At 21 he sailed to Spain and never returned. He served in the army, then settled in Andalusia and turned to writing.

His main works:

  • La Florida (1605), on the expedition of Hernando de Soto in North America
  • the Royal Commentaries of the Incas (1609), on Inca history, religion, laws and customs
  • the General History of Peru (1617), on the Spanish conquest

His books gave a proud, ordered picture of the Incas. In the 1780s, after the revolt of Túpac Amaru II, Spain banned the Commentaries in Peru for fear they would feed rebellion. He died in Córdoba in 1616.
